findings.description: The 'data' bucket has no ACL set to private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment states the bucket is public. Anonymous readers could reach the sensitive object stored in it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects including customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No logging block is configured, so access to this publicly exposed bucket is not recorded, preventing detection or forensic investigation of unauthorized data access.

A file named 'customer-master.xlsx' containing apparent customer master data is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible aws_s3_bucket.data, and the object itself sets no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy change can expose sensitive financial data publicly with no account/bucket-level guardrail.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, leaving no audit trail of object access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data in the operations bucket is not encrypted at rest with a managed key.
No logging block is configured, so no S3 server access log records exist for this bucket to support intrusion detection or forensics.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose its contents publicly without a guardrail.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored datasets unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could make datasets publicly readable with no account/bucket-level guardrail.

The central log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and relies solely on the log-delivery-write ACL; without public access blocking, log data could be exposed by a later ACL or policy change.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached, so objects in this public bucket may be requested over plaintext HTTP.
No bucket policy denying non-TLS requests is attached, so financial objects may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

The logs bucket uses force_destroy = true and has no object lock or MFA delete, so an actor with bucket-level permissions can destroy the audit trail that other buckets depend on, undermining log integrity.
